stem: An ideal Zener diode of breakdown voltage $8$ V is connected with an $800\ \Omega$ load and a $400\ \Omega$ series resistor across an $18$ V supply, as shown in the figure. Its power dissipation is

verdicts.working: With the Zener in breakdown, the output is 8 V. The series current is (18−8)/400 = 25 mA; the load current is 8/800 = 10 mA. Thus the Zener current is 15 mA and its power is 8 × 15 mA = 120 mW.

notes: figure check: The Zener diode is reversed: its cathode (the bar/hook end of the symbol) is drawn at the bottom toward the common return instead of at the output node, contradicting the brief (cathode at output node, anode at bottom).; The Zener diode label is missing the breakdown voltage: it is labeled only 'Zener' with no '8 V' value.; The output node label V_out is present but the bottom common-return 'Zener/common' labels overlap the wire/nodes slightly; 'Zener' text sits on the bottom wire.

Independent check: With the Zener in breakdown, the output is 8 V. The series current is (18−8)/400 = 25 mA; the load current is 8/800 = 10 mA. Thus the Zener current is 15 mA and its power is 8 × 15 mA = 120 mW.
solution:
In breakdown, $V_o=V_Z=8\text{ V}$. The series and load currents are
$$I_s=\frac{18-8}{400}=25\text{ mA},\qquad I_L=\frac{8}{800}=10\text{ mA}.$$
Hence $I_Z=I_s-I_L=15\text{ mA}$, so $P_Z=V_ZI_Z=8(15\text{ mA})=120\text{ mW}$.

From the positive terminal, draw a $400\ \Omega$ resistor in series to an output node. From the output node to the bottom return wire, draw two parallel branches: one branch contains an $800\ \Omega$ load resistor; the other contains an ideal Zener diode with breakdown voltage $8$ V, with its cathode connected to the output node and its anode connected to the bottom return. Label the source, series resistor, load resistor, Zener diode, output node, and common return.
